title: Testing your node without a GPU

questions.q: What is the quickest way to test that a V3 node's maths is right?
options: Call execute directly with a small tensor
Start a server and queue a graph
Render a picture on a card
questions.answer: Call execute directly with a small tensor
questions.why: It is a classmethod, so no engine is needed. We ran one this way.

questions.q: Which bug can't a direct call of a V1 function catch?
questions.why: The direct call just hands back x. In the engine, merge_result_data fails on an int, and a tensor silently loses its first axis.

questions.q: A real run fails inside your test harness. Where do you find the error?
options: ex.status_messages holds an execution_error, and ex.success is False
questions.answer: ex.status_messages holds an execution_error, and ex.success is False
questions.why: The executor catches the exception and sends a message. A test that doesn't look at it passes wrongly.

questions.q: How do you test that a fingerprint works?
options: Queue twice in one executor and count runs
Create a new executor for each queue
questions.answer: Queue twice in one executor and count runs
questions.why: The cache lives in the executor. A new one starts empty, so it would always run.

questions.q: What can't you test on a CPU with tiny tensors?
options: Whether real weights give a good picture
questions.answer: Whether real weights give a good picture
questions.why: Speed, memory use and quality need the real model and usually the card.
